title: What If the Sun's Gravity Vanished but It Kept Shining?

scenes.text: What if the Sun's gravity switched off? You wouldn't notice for eight minutes.
Gravity travels at the speed of light, so Earth keeps orbiting for about eight minutes and twenty seconds.
Then Earth stops curving and flies straight ahead at about nineteen miles every second.
No jolt, and the Moon stays with us. The Sun still shines, but every day it looks smaller.
After a year, Earth would be roughly six hundred million miles away, with sunlight about forty times weaker.
Without the pull, the Sun's light is only a memory. Eight minutes is all gravity needs to say goodbye.

description:
What if the Sun's gravity switched off but it kept shining?
Earth would fly off in a straight line at about nineteen miles a second after eight minutes.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Would you rather lose the Sun's light or its gravity? Drop your own 'what if' too.
